        Pursuant to sections 203(a)(1) and (2) of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”) 1 and Part 33 of

the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (the “Commission”) regulations, 2 Tom Sawyer

Solar, LLC (“Tom Sawyer Solar”) and Union Electric Company d/b/a Ameren Missouri (“Ameren

Missouri”) (together, “Applicants”) respectfully submit this Application requesting approval for

transactions that will result in Ameren Missouri operating a 175 MW AC solar-powered electric

generation facility (the “Facility”) to serve its load.

        Applicants respectfully request that the Commission issue an order approving the Proposed

Transactions (defined below) within ninety (90) days of this Application, by September 13, 2026,

as this will provide the Applicants regulatory certainty as they move forward with the Proposed

Transactions.

     I.   EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

         The Proposed Transactions effectuate the construction of new generation to serve Ameren

Missouri’s retail customers. Ameren Missouri has entered into a Build Transfer Agreement

pursuant to which EDF power solutions Development, Inc. (“EDFpsDI”) will construct the

Facility, inclusive of the gen-tie line between the project substation and the point of

interconnection for Ameren Missouri and to Ameren Missouri’s specifications. The Facility will

be located in the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) balancing authority

area (“BAA”).

         As described further herein, after the Facility achieves mechanical completion, Ameren

Missouri will acquire the Facility through a two-step transaction (“BTA-Related Transaction”).

First, Ameren Missouri will acquire 100 percent of the membership interests in Tom Sawyer Solar

from EDFpsDI for the purchase price set forth in the Build Transfer Agreement (“Step 1”). That

is, EDFpsDI will transfer all of its membership interests in Tom Sawyer Solar to Ameren Missouri,

after which EDFpsDI will no longer have any ownership interests in Tom Sawyer Solar. Following

closing on Step 1, Tom Sawyer Solar will merge with and into Ameren Missouri (“Step 2”).

         In addition to the BTA-Related Transaction, Ameren Missouri seeks approval to lease the

Facility from Audrain County, Missouri (“Audrain County”) pursuant to Sections 100.010 to

100.200 of the Revised Statues of Missouri and Article VI, Section 27(b) of the Missouri

Constitution (collectively, “Chapter 100”) (the “Lease Transaction,” and with the BTA-Related

Transaction, the “Proposed Transactions”). 3 Tom Sawyer Solar has entered into an agreement to

    II.   REQUEST FOR PRIVILEGED TREATMENT

          Pursuant to sections 33.8 and 388.112 of the Commission’s regulations, 6 Applicants

request privileged and confidential treatment for the Build Transfer Agreement contained in

Exhibit I and the map in Exhibit K. Applicants are providing the information in Exhibits I and K

with the understanding that it will remain non-public. This information is commercially sensitive

Applicants also request privileged treatment for certain confidential or proprietary commercial

data included in the workpapers associated with the Solomon/Opgrand Affidavit. These exhibits

and workpapers are not publicly available and are exempt from the mandatory public disclosure

requirements of the Freedom of Information Act.7 The release of such information would disclose

IV.    THE PROPOSED TRANSACTIONS AND AFFECTED JURISDICTIONAL
       FACILITIES

       The cumulative result of the Proposed Transactions will be Ameren Missouri’s operation

and control of the Facility, with the Facility incorporated with Ameren Missouri’s overall

generation fleet to serve load. Applicants respectfully request that the Commission issue an order

approving the Proposed Transactions within ninety (90) days of this Application, by September

13, 2026. Applicants request Commission action by this date so they have regulatory certainty

that will allow them to move forward with the development of the Facility.

       The Commission-jurisdictional assets involved in the Proposed Transactions include the

Facility, Tom Sawyer Solar’s market-based rate tariff, and the limited and discrete interconnection

facilities owned by Tom Sawyer Solar (once operational and used to transmit power in interstate

commerce) that are necessary to interconnect the Facility to the transmission system, and various

books and records.

                     1.    The Proposed Transactions Do Not Raise Horizontal Market Power
                           Issues

       The Commission’s Merger Policy Statement requires an analysis of the competitive effects

of a proposed transfer that examines the effect of that transfer on horizontal market concentration. 31

Under the Commission’s regulations, a horizontal competitive screen analysis is required “if, as a

result of the proposed transaction, a single corporate entity obtains ownership or control over the

generating facilities of previously unaffiliated merging entities.” 32 A horizontal market power

analysis is not required if the applicant “[a]ffirmatively demonstrates that the merging entities do

not currently conduct business in the same geographic markets or that the extent of the business

        The Proposed Transactions are akin to a self-build project by Ameren Missouri. Unlike a

change-in-control transaction, the Facility will be a new generating asset entering the MISO

market. Consequently, although transfers are taking place, they are not transfers from an entity

that previously operated the Facility in the MISO market. Pursuant to the Build Transfer

Agreement, EDF is constructing the Facility for Ameren Missouri, to be transferred to Ameren

Missouri on a “turnkey” basis.34 Ameren Missouri is to acquire Tom Sawyer Solar (the Facility

project company) after the Facility’s mechanical completion, i.e., prior to commercial operation.

Thus, Tom Sawyer Solar and Ameren Missouri will never separately conduct business within the

same geographic market. Similarly, after close on the BTA-Related Transaction, the Facility will

be under Ameren Missouri’s control at all times even after the Lease Transaction. Ameren

Missouri will own the Facility before it is commercially operational, and after the Facility is

conveyed to Audrain County as passive lessor, Ameren Missouri will continue to control the

Facility pursuant to the terms of the lease. Such transactions are inherently less concerning from

 Exhibit M – Cross Subsidization Analysis


The Commission’s regulations require that FPA section 203 applicants show that their proposed
transaction will not, at the time of the transaction or in the future, result in:

       1) any transfer of facilities between a traditional public utility associate company that has
       captive customers or that owns or provides transmission service over jurisdictional
       transmission facilities, and an associate company;

       (2) any new issuance of securities by a traditional public utility associate company that has
       captive customers or that owns, or provides transmission service over, jurisdictional
       transmission facilities, for the benefit of an associate company;
       (3) any new pledge or encumbrance of assets of a traditional public utility associate
       company that has captive customers or that owns or provides transmission service over
       jurisdictional transmission facilities, for the benefit of an associate company; or
       (4) any new affiliate contract between a nonutility associate company and a traditional
       public utility associate company that has captive customers or that owns or provides
       transmission service over jurisdictional transmission facilities, other than non-power goods
       and services agreements subject to review under sections 205 and 206 of the Federal Power
       Act.

       As demonstrated below, the Proposed Transactions will not result in inappropriate cross-
subsidization and are in the public interest.
        First, the transfer by EDF of the ownership interests in Tom Sawyer Solar to Ameren
pursuant to the BTA-Related Transaction is not a sale of facilities between a traditional public utility
associate company that has captive customers and an associate company because EDF is not an
associate company of Ameren Missouri. Immediately following the closing of Step 1 of the BTA-
Related Transaction, Tom Sawyer Solar will ultimately merge with and into Ameren Missouri (and
not Ameren Corporation). Additionally, the sale-leaseback arrangement between Audrain County
and Ameren Missouri is also not a sale of facilities between a traditional public utility associate
company that has captive customers and an associate company because Audrain County is not an
associate company of Ameren Missouri; Audrain County will be a passive owner-lessor, and
Ameren Missouri will operate and control the Facility. Any benefits relating to the financial
performance of the Facility will flow to the regulated utility, Ameren Missouri, for the benefit of its
customers.
        Second, the Proposed Transactions will not result in any new issuance of securities by a
traditional public utility for the benefit of an associate company. At the time of the filing of this
Application, as explained in Section III.A of the Application, prior to closing on the BTA-Related
Transaction, Tom Sawyer Solar is a direct, wholly-owned subsidiary of EDF. Neither Tom Sawyer
Solar nor EDF is a traditional public utility or has captive customers or transmission customers.
No new securities will be issued by Ameren Missouri for the benefit of an associate company in
connection with the Proposed Transactions.

         Third, the Proposed Transactions will not result in any new pledge by a traditional public
utility for the benefit of an associate company. At the time of the filing of this Application, Tom
Sawyer Solar does not own any utility assets and as explained in Section III.A of the Application,

prior to closing on the BTA-Related Transaction, it is a direct, wholly-owned subsidiary of EDF.
Neither Tom Sawyer Solar nor EDF is a traditional public utility or has captive customers or
transmission customers. The Proposed Transactions will not result in any new pledge or
encumbrance of the assets of Ameren Missouri for the benefit of an associate company. Ameren
Missouri has the financial ability to construct the Facility through the Build Transfer Agreement.
Although Audrain County will be the passive owner-lessor of the Facility, this ownership structure
will benefit Ameren Missouri and its retail ratepayers by enabling it to lower the Facility’s costs
through certain tax savings.

        Fourth, the Proposed Transactions will not result in any new affiliate contracts between a
nonutility associate company and a traditional public utility associate company. As to the BTA-
Related Transaction, the Build Transfer Agreement is between non-affiliates, and Tom Sawyer
Solar will not become an affiliate of Ameren Missouri until after the Step 1 of the BTA-Related
Transaction occurs. Immediately upon closing or shortly after Step 1 of the BTA-Related
Transaction closes, Tom Sawyer Solar will merge with and into Ameren Missouri. As for the sale-
leaseback arrangement with Audrain County, Audrain County is not an affiliate of Ameren
Missouri and will not become one as a part of the Proposed Transactions; it will only be the passive
owner-lessor of the Facility. Thus, no new affiliate transactions occur in connection with the
Proposed Transactions. As a result, the Commission should find that the Proposed Transactions
are in the public interest and will not result in any inappropriate cross-subsidization.
